tasks.title: Deliver shared operations and durable workspace state
acceptance: Human and AI actions use the same registry, permissions, confirmations, revisions and idempotency semantics.
Workspace restoration and undo preserve accepted state; restart does not replay prior AI operations.
Introduce versioned database migrations and recovery tests when persistent state is first introduced.

A user-selected local decision note retains the dated rationale and evidence references across restart. Append later outcomes separately. Exercise deletion and recovery, and verify that declining to save leaves no decision note.

Exercise commit, lost reply, concurrent replay, fresh disclosure authorization, target selection conflict, undo and rollback. Verify note deletion across restart and restoration with and without known deletion markers.

Provide an explicitly enabled Ubuntu development entry for versioned workspace operations. Exercise a local authorized change, undo and restart against the same Rust authorization and persistence core. Keep the existing synthetic history-only grant restricted and keep the Windows release target.

Keep saved conversation content, memory, strategy material and derived indexes in the active local user profile. Test two distinct user profiles, local backup and recovery, deletion and cache cleanup. Opening one profile or restoring an older copy never reveals the other user’s data or restores an outbound excerpt grant.

plan.outcome: An authorized human or AI change goes through the same Rust registry, survives process restart in the originating local profile and can be undone by operation ID. Accepted results, private records and deletion decisions survive the documented recovery cases. The next slice proves current local human or scoped on-device AI can change the main chart timeframe under independently versioned shared evidence, recover one authorized receipt after a lost response, and undo an eligible chart edit. In the profile-local private-record slice, the owner can explicitly save, list, inspect, correct and delete a titled typed exchange with ordered speakers, a memory or a strategy. The same records reopen after a restart in that profile. A local backup can recover missing records and preserve known deletions.
hypotheses: Start with 1m to 5m, restart the Rust process, undo by the returned operation ID and restart to 1m. Two profiles with the same workspace ID make isolation directly observable.
A profile-bound, long-lived Rust core can share one transaction owner across the native and explicitly enabled Ubuntu workspace entries.

A synthetic original thesis and a separately dated outcome can be distinguished after restart. Deleting their note can retain a profile-bound marker and redacted operation results without leaving the body available to a live read, undo or idempotent replay.
A logical backup limited to decision notes can recover missing originals and dated outcomes, keep newer work, and suppress marked notes without copying operation history, grants or SQLite journals.

Restore stages can retain only pending inserts and release them when the revision changes, a deadline expires or the session ends. Revision-based projection refresh can preserve a surviving note's unsubmitted outcome draft while clearing deleted list entries and details.

The published single-series CSV revision UUID identifies the frozen chart and scopes its instrument identity. Derive the history-chain-v1 hash from the exact stored bars. Use the exclusive bar-start coverage bound as the deterministic cutoff for this closed-bar source, which carries no observation clock.

Native publication browsing can use stored v5 revision summaries while v6 selection and projected chart reads continue through scoped workspace permissions. Opening a library row follows the same revocation checks as opening by revision ID.

An already submitted deletion can retain only its original scope, challenge and opaque record ID after the detail disappears. Retry recovers the original body-free receipt or returns a current terminal denial. Exercise a dropped committed reply, BUSY during post-commit WAL cleanup, and BUSY before commit followed by a peer rename using actual Chromium and SQLite.

Two real browser windows sharing a workspace must clear unavailable private bodies and invalid reviews. If a peer corrects a record that remains authorized, preserve the local draft and explicitly review it against the current record. Independent pending approvals on one writer are bounded and cancellation is scoped to the exact challenge. Restore reports all current surviving records, including those absent from the archive.

A private records panel reachable from the native and enabled Ubuntu workspace serves all three types through one typed read and write contract. Manual capture keeps existing transient conversation and speech flows independent.
A bounded logical private-record archive can merge missing records and the union of known tombstones without retaining prior bodies, outbound grants or a secondary search index.

Use the workspace revision and the selected record revision for correction and deletion. A revision-bound local approval stages only the pending changes. Committing and replaying use a random challenge with no private body or fingerprint in the approval request, log or receipt. The state-migrations gate runs the persistence suite without a name filter. It covers genuine v1–v7 fixtures, rollback and reopen, private archive recovery, deletion cleanup and refusal of restored approval or outbound access.

risks.failure: A lost response, concurrent duplicate or stale selected target applies a change twice or reveals a result after grants change.
A crash during migration or restore exposes a half-applied workspace, revives a known deleted note, or carries a grant into a different local profile.
A private body is retained in a receipt, undo payload, index, app-controlled export or log after deletion.
The bundled database or a Rust module dependency cannot be built on a supported target, or the locked license and advisory inventory no longer matches the delivered code.
A new browser loses the eligible undo, an ordinary startup obtains a workspace writer, or a suspended request replays twice.
An old token becomes valid again after reopen, a second writer overwrites an intervening choice, or a revoked dataset or grant discloses private chart data.
Revocation leaves an old chart, provenance, bars or projection visible, an older response restores the bytes, or the unavailable target cannot be cleared without its revoked display right.
A foreign profile, model route or paired client can read saved bodies, or a backup reuses outbound approval.
A stale approval overwrites another edit, or a failed transaction commits a partial private record or tombstone.
A correction or deletion leaves superseded pages in SQLite sidecars, or an older archive revives a known deletion.

plan.rollback: Keep the selected backup file untouched. Stage a revision-bound restore in memory. Cancel, reject or interrupt before committing the SQLite transaction and verify the previous live notes, deletion state and timeframe remain available across process restart. Exercise v6 migration rollback and a rejected selection transaction against a populated v5 fixture, then reopen and verify both revisions, undo, notes, mappings and published data. Bind private-record approval and restore preview to the same revision. On failure roll back SQLite and preserve the selected backup. Exercise a failed write and an interrupted migration on disposable databases, verify clean restart, and retry only after rereading the current revision. Reopen and restore the populated v7 fixture through the v8 migration. Preserve the exact prior ledger, folder manifest, source bytes, prior note and chart state when v8 rolls back.

non_goals: The first backup covers saved decision notes, dated outcomes and deletion markers. Broader workspace settings, accepted indicator versions, saved conversations, credentials, grants, audit history, caches and journals are outside this backup format.
Real cloud or voice sessions, financial provider subscriptions, and full indicator computation belong to other tasks.

The chart evidence slice uses the registered main chart and the existing published CSV interval. It adds no selection kinds, provider transmission, external recipient admission or confirmation surface.

The separate private-record archive excludes notes, ephemeral chat and speech, prompts, audio, model sessions, provider calls, automated extraction and outbound attachment grants. No search index is required for the bounded list and detail reads.

preserve: Synthetic read-only development grant, existing 1.1 reads, explicitly selected sample preferences, established confirmation and private excerpt rules.
Keep ordinary connected-model scope and the exact selected excerpt rule independent of saving. Preserve the v6 ledger and the genuine v7 folder migration.
change: The private hosts dispatch decisionNote.save, decisionNote.read, decisionNote.appendOutcome and decisionNote.delete through the Rust registry. Explicit local confirmation authorizes new writes. Reads and redacted receipt replay use current disclosure access.

Add explicit local decision-note export and revision-bound preview and apply. Recover missing notes and outcomes, preserve other current notes, reject conflicting surviving identities and apply the union of known deletion markers in the same transaction. Warn before approving candidates whose deletion history is unavailable.
Check complete backup capacity before admitting note additions and restore plans. Keep private drafts separate from refreshed note projections.

Add a shared chart interval and an independently increasing selection token; local hover and chart navigation stay in the UI. Recheck current target access and exact requested fields for projected reads.

Revalidate the main-chart target and both revision tokens for new chart edits. Require an effective local chart analysis grant for AI mutations using a selected interval. Rebuild chart-only replay results from the immutable receipt under current workspace disclosure.

Invalidate the open published revision and pending old replies after observing current display entitlement loss. Keep unavailable selection clear controls reachable from both the workspace and the revision dialog.

Add private-record save, inspection, correction and deletion to the trusted local registry with one shared editor for conversation exchanges, memories and strategies. Add a separate explicit local backup and revision-bound restore preview.
evolution.data_plan: Keep application state inside the bound OS-user profile. The v1 to v2 migration retains chart state, undo and replay and adds immutable originals, separate outcomes and profile-scoped deletion markers. Version 3 preserves outcome order and supports several outcomes under one restore receipt. A versioned logical note backup stays scoped to its originating profile and workspace. Version 6 adds only the selected immutable revision UUID and interval bounds. It preserves the existing selection revision and all workspace, undo, note, mapping, publication and revocation records. The reference restores no disclosure grant. Add v8 with a bound private-record table, body-free replay metadata and tombstones. Use one SQLite transaction for the workspace revision, receipt and record change. The logical archive retains current record bodies and tombstone IDs only.
evolution.cleanup: Delete original and outcome bodies, clear body-derived replay fingerprints, and durably resume SQLite WAL cleanup if a reader blocks it. Restore without replaying past AI work or reusing external disclosure grants. Clear the selected reference explicitly without resetting its token. Deny a revoked target without restoring or exporting its contents. Securely replace or delete superseded private record bodies and checkpoint SQLite WAL with durable retry. Release browser drafts and approval stages on cancel, supersession and close. Warn about independent older copies.

A bounded, typed declarative evaluator and independent preview lifetime can run before the durable layout checkpoint lands.

Bind trusted Python dispatch to the one-time local decision, exact selected code, resolved parameters, immutable input, scope revisions and affirmative source-purpose rights. Keep runner output untrusted until the registry verifies the full artifact.

tasks.title: Deliver the first human-AI chart collaboration workflow
acceptance: Mock AI uses actual chart context and core tools to create, inspect and revise an indicator draft.
Cancellation and authorization apply to every tool execution, and claims refer to actual results.
Record model, prompt, tool and input versions when they first affect reproducibility; preserve replayable evaluation scenarios.
Mock acceptance is separate from later real-model and real-data usability validation.

From a selected interval, reveal a versioned row or local document passage in another view, highlight the exact evidence and continue after the user corrects the range. Preserve the previous view and surface stale or missing anchors.

Observe the target and actual core result in the affected chart, column or panel. Check denial, cancellation and stale revisions, and exercise a layout edit through the same core operation as a manual edit.
Suggest a local CSV mapping from permitted sample fields. Show the proposal for correction and run the approved deterministic rule with the same result as a manually supplied mapping.

From a buy question, compare two explanations using workspace data and a reproducible calculation. Show contrary evidence and update the conclusion when the user corrects a premise. Seek clarification about a possible behavioral pattern. The discussion itself authorizes no mutation.

In the same conversation, carry out a separately scoped chart action. Offer to save the user's choice, including inaction, with the original evidence and disagreement. Reopen the note after a later price move, assess reasoning using information known at the time and surface any data or execution defect separately.

Correlate interleaved tool calls and terminal outcomes; selection changes, pending confirmations and cancellation preserve attributable committed effects. A first question on an unconfigured model offers configuration or an explicit labeled mock without dispatch.

Exercise portable provider settings, source and purpose disclosure, consent, denial, microphone stop and revocation on Ubuntu with explicit local fixtures. No paid or Windows-only connection is needed for these local cases. Real text and duplex qualification and native credentials retain independent release gates.

Through the normal UI and final request builder, activate a disclosed route once and complete successive ordinary turns and authorized tool calls with no repeated consent. A saved conversation, memory or strategy adds only the exact selected excerpt for its named request and recipient. Exercise edits, cancellation, previous-turn attachments, other users, restore and revoked grants, including a provider conversation handle that would otherwise retain private context.

Offer only granted local profiling, mapping preview and validation tools. Compare the AI-produced rule with the offline manual rule. The model sees only the selected permitted fields and never receives a credential or authority to execute arbitrary transformations.

A hung check loses diagnostics or leaves child processes running.
An inherited dependency alias hides a forbidden architecture edge.

tasks.title: Establish deterministic market fixtures before chart integration
acceptance: Commit synthetic fixtures with fixed time and seed for the three specified instruments and timeframes.
Verify OHLC, timestamps, gaps, partial bars and trading-day boundaries against independent expected values.

plan.outcome: Commit reproducible synthetic histories and partial-bar replay snapshots for all three specified instruments and timeframes, with independent numerical and calendar oracles and an executable market-fixtures gate.
hypotheses: A pure Python generator using integer price ticks, fixed seeds and explicit UTC sample sessions can supply repeatable inputs to the upcoming chart workflow without extra dependencies or real provider access.
Explicit synthetic trading-day assignments and session anchors prevent UTC-date grouping and gap filling from corrupting five-minute and daily bars.
A fixture-only change type can bind this prerequisite to implemented checks while retaining runtime recovery as a separate, visibly unimplemented M1-003 requirement.

risks.failure: Self-confirming generated expectations hide incorrect OHLC, null volume propagation, session alignment or trading-day grouping.
Missing observations fabricate bars, partial updates create duplicate keys, or a stalled partial bar is silently finalized.
Host time, timezone, random state or caller mutation changes replay data or its source identity.
Fixture integration changes accepted records, crosses worker boundaries or claims chart/recovery acceptance prematurely.

plan.rollback: Retain failed reports and golden inputs; repair the generator or oracle against independently calculated expectations, never refresh expectations just to make checks pass. Revert this isolated provider/fixture slice if needed and keep M1-001 and M1-003 unverified until their actual workflows are implemented.

tasks.title: Verify market interruption and recovery through the chart
acceptance: Make interruption, staleness and bounded recovery visible.
Reconnect without duplicate subscriptions and preserve final bar state under update coalescing.

plan.outcome: A user can see a worker interruption, retain the last verified bar and recover without duplicated subscriptions. A missing closed bar appears only after a bounded, verified backfill, or the gap stays visible.
hypotheses: Keep the confirmed series, snapshot, epoch, sequence, observation and boundary bar in one Rust-owned logical subscription across worker replacement. A fresh negotiation can reproduce the confirmed synthetic boundary before replay resumes.
The chart can apply a verified repaired range while keeping its original frozen input available for inspection.

risks.failure: An epoch change, duplicate or superseded selection splices unrelated updates or starts a second active worker.
Recovery loses a closed bar, hides uncertainty or mutates the frozen history used for comparison.
A process test kills the wrong worker or an injected recovery is mistaken for a real process recovery.
A cropped interval hides a known gap, a replacement changes already closed history, or a worker exit during repair hides disconnection.
The same row digest hides changed visible coverage or a structurally valid repair frame carries different bars from its declared digest.

plan.rollback: Retain the failed event trace from synthetic data, stop the replacement worker, preserve the last validated bar and show the unresolved gap. A known-good frozen chart remains available while the recovery path is repaired.

non_goals: Real feeds, persisted subscriptions, trading, and product fault-injection controls.

preserve: Finite sample replay, exact confirmed epochs and sequences, single-worker admission, independent quality facts and immutable source history.
change: Exercise child replacement, bounded re-handshake, verified backfill and cancellation on one logical subscription.
evolution.data_plan: Recovery state belongs to the active subscription in local memory. Do not persist user input or add grants.
evolution.cleanup: Release old process handles before starting a replacement; one cancellation stops pending recovery, backoff and subsequent frames.

plan.rollback: Revert the new workflow tooling while preserving checkpoints, accepted records and per-run evidence; repair hosted failures before advancing integration.

tasks.title: Audit the scaffold for sustained product delivery and extensibility

hypotheses: Existing local records and checks are a useful foundation, but consistency checks alone cannot establish behavioral correctness.
Targeted correction and early vertical product slices are preferable to adding speculative workflow infrastructure.

Audit probes contaminate working source or historical evidence.

tasks.title: Close verification subprocess lifetimes on every completion path
acceptance: Successful and nonzero root exits cannot leave check-owned descendants running or writing after the final log digest is recorded.
Timeout and interruption diagnostics remain retained; verify cleanup with actual bounded child processes on Linux and Windows.
Document the trusted-process boundary without claiming a hostile-code sandbox.

plan.outcome: A check cannot leave descendants running or writing after root success, failure, timeout or interruption; cleanup failures remain failed verification.
hypotheses: POSIX process-group cleanup can run after normal root exit and wait for surviving members to stop.
A Windows Job Object assigned before releasing a gated launcher owns descendants even after the command root exits.

risks.failure: Windows children start before job assignment or survive normal parent exit.

tasks.title: Repair market, operation and acceptance contracts from the full review
acceptance: Both manifests, canonical wire definitions, generated projections, delivery plans and acceptance rules resolve the full contract review. Every reviewed outcome has an identified implementation or acceptance gate.

The current history entry, registry and preview produce correct metadata, bounded reproducible input, usable startup and actionable errors. Independent vectors and end-to-end checks cover regressions.
Project verification distinguishes partial and whole workflows, effective owner decisions, real and mock observations, native platform acceptance and the exact release candidate.

plan.outcome: An implementer can complete every reviewed journey with consistent wire objects and verification gates; each current failure has a tested repair.
hypotheses: Existing read-only registry and preview can retain legacy reads while gaining immutable inputs. Portable workflows and real-session qualification can have independent gates.

risks.failure: New contracts cannot round-trip in one of the three generated bindings or mix observations across pages.
A chart or acceptance route shows a successful but stale, unconfigured or unauthorized result.

plan.rollback: Preserve historical receipts and prior accepted ADRs. Revert the coherent source checkpoint if compatibility checks fail and retain the failing report.

non_goals: Implementing planned market subscriptions, persistence, AI sessions or trading merely to register their contract.

preserve: Existing supported synthetic reads, historical task receipts and centralized authorization.
change: Repair ambiguous identities, authorization, lifecycle, source restoration and release verification.
evolution.data_plan: Use synthetic input for all regressions. Persist only an explicit local sample preference in the current preview. Specify migration and recovery for future persisted user data.
evolution.cleanup: Replace the broken entry and ambiguous contracts, regenerate all projections and verify history, checks and support claims.

tasks.title: Keep staged replacements verifiable across multiple revisions
acceptance: A review from either an original or intermediate Git revision follows each recorded replacement through to all its current required checks. Missing coverage, cycles and unreviewed changes fail.

Completed or cancelled plans retain their original work classification after its retirement. Every unfinished plan still uses current classifications, and every current capability has a surviving current delivery task.
Developers can find the repair owner, a proportionate staged cutover and recovery procedure, and the condition for resuming the product task in the existing development and delivery policies.

plan.outcome: Change implementation or checks over several independently verifiable steps while preserving active product commitments, historical receipts and the next product task.
hypotheses: The history check currently considers only immediate replacements. Classification validation consults current delivery policy for historical tasks. Separate cancellation and scope checks can hide a surviving requirement.

risks.failure: One branch of a split check disappears or a circular replacement is counted as coverage.
A historical record blocks removal of obsolete implementation policy or a current capability loses its accountable work.

plan.rollback: Retain the failing isolated fixture and original Git checkpoint. Revert the tooling change as a unit if it accepts weaker coverage. Resume M1-006 after verification.

non_goals: Creating a second planning system, changing product behavior or performing a production data migration.

preserve: Existing task and receipt formats, immutable accepted history, single-step check replacements, current required checks and product scope.
change: Resolve chains of reviewed gate replacements across revisions, retire unused work classifications and distinguish available delivery from cancelled work.
evolution.data_plan: Exercise versioned synthetic repositories. Product persistence and wire formats are unchanged.
evolution.cleanup: Reuse the existing task graph, gate records and check commands. Restore focus to M1-006 after evidence is recorded.

tasks.title: Run development in Herdr and bind model use to local user content boundaries
acceptance: A developer can launch a bounded task in Herdr using the requested implementation or supervision model. Parallel writers have explicit ownership, one integrator and verified results. Ordinary changes and necessary tooling installation proceed under the existing owner grant.

Local conversations, memory, strategies and their derived data have accountable storage, recovery and downstream-use requirements. Activating a model grants ordinary in-session use within the disclosed scope. Sharing saved private content uses only the selected preview for the named destination.

Automated qualification distinguishes ordinary chat from private excerpt transfer, and retained verification artifacts exclude unrelated personal files. Product implementation and real model acceptance stay attributable to the product tasks.

plan.outcome: A new development session can start its own Herdr implementation and review work while protecting local product records and keeping ordinary connected-model turns usable.
hypotheses: The installed Herdr core can run the actual repository and both requested Codex model profiles without changing account defaults. Existing evidence collection and model authorization need a distinction between routine requests and saved private content.

risks.failure: A helper changes someone else’s work or a launcher silently substitutes the wrong model.
A cloud route receives saved history or the evidence upload includes a private record.

plan.rollback: Keep the existing local checks and prior delivery evidence. Retain any failed isolated fixture, revert the affected tooling change, and leave product runtime connections disabled until qualified.

non_goals: Implementing a complete storage engine, provisioning a paid product model, or exporting real product content in scaffold tests.

preserve: A fresh offline chart, specific third-party source rights, provider choice and existing local verification commands.
change: Adopt Herdr for active development and one-time cloud connection scope with separate approval for selected saved private excerpts.
evolution.data_plan: Use repository code and synthetic fixtures for all development, subprocess and hosted verification. Keep owned product records and backups in local application storage.
evolution.cleanup: Reuse the task ledger and native Herdr terminals. Inspect delivered changes, retire only owned temporary sessions and restore the product focus.

tasks.title: Correct synthetic market freshness and read explicit quality revisions
acceptance: Derive freshness from the declared observation schedule, cutoff and source delay independently of known gaps or loss of connection. A scheduled close, old historical date or missing evidence alone never implies stale. Preserve existing normal snapshot hashes and normal legacy metadata semantics.

Read the known explicit stale and gapped fixture revisions through the existing versioned history request, retain exact series and snapshot identity, and reject unknown revisions. A known stale series with a gap preserves both facts under the legacy gapped summary.

plan.outcome: Consumers of a frozen history page can distinguish coverage and freshness and explicitly replay the supplied sample revision through the existing operation.
hypotheses: A typed expectation for the synthetic sample and a bounded mapping to its revisions suffice without a new operation or provider. The data change can be completed independently of the replay UI.

risks.failure: A gap hides a missed update or missing evidence invents an open or stale state.
A pinned sample silently resolves to different bars or a normal snapshot changes.

plan.rollback: Retain failed vectors and revert the affected sample selector or derivation. No user files or stored data need migration.

non_goals: Real market access, UI presentation, native process lifetime and subscription transport.

preserve: Normal 1.0 and 1.1 synthetic history, stable frozen bar digests and explicit sample opt-in.
change: Derive independent freshness and coverage and honor recognized explicitly pinned quality revisions.
evolution.data_plan: Existing frozen normal inputs keep their identities. Only checked-in synthetic data is involved.
evolution.cleanup: Use a single quality derivation and remove reliance on a legacy display label as input.

tasks.title: Preserve failure diagnostics on Windows consoles
acceptance: A failed check containing Unicode outside the console encoding retains its diagnostic log and returns the original failed check result so the run can finalize and stage evidence. Receipt hashes still bind the original bytes.

plan.outcome: A check failure is diagnosable from the finalized run even on a legacy Windows console.
hypotheses: The failure occurs only when the diagnostic tail is printed. Keeping raw bytes in the log and encoding a short console result safely preserves both diagnostics and the failed gate.

risks.failure: Reporting raises a second exception and hides the original failure, or a private stdout is printed.

plan.rollback: Retain the hosted console and local recovery snapshot. Run the affected check with its isolated log while repairing the harness, then rerun native verification.

non_goals: Mask the failed product check, change the process timeout or claim physical Windows acceptance.

preserve: Original raw check-log bytes, digest, exit code and redacted private check output.
change: Console diagnostics remain parseable even when their text includes characters outside its code page.
evolution.data_plan: No stored product data changes. Existing reports stay readable.
evolution.cleanup: Use the existing structured harness output and keep a single private-log policy.

tasks.title: Align shared-selection and durable mutation revision requirements
acceptance: The product rule, human request and AI tool intent agree on the independent selection and durable workspace revision preconditions. Shared vectors reject substitution of either revision for the other and preserve valid 1.1 callers.

plan.outcome: A developer implementing shared selection or a selection-bound durable write can identify the right revision without changing protocol 1.1 payloads.
hypotheses: The wire structs already encode both forms of optimistic concurrency. The broad AI policy sentence disagrees with the specific selection contract.

risks.failure: Requiring a workspace revision for selection rejects valid clients, or substituting a selection token for the durable revision allows a stale mutation.

plan.rollback: Retain the accepted 1.1 schemas and regression vectors. Revisit the policy and add a versioned change only if existing callers actually require a different wire shape.

non_goals: Implement durable storage, authorize a new actor, change wire identifiers or mark any planned workspace operation implemented.

preserve: Wire 1.1 human and AI requests, current grant checks, and independent selection tokens.
change: Make the revision requirement for each operation explicit and exercise wrong-token substitution.
evolution.data_plan: No saved or transmitted data format changes.
evolution.cleanup: Replace the conflicting blanket instruction with the rules already used by the registered commands.

tasks.title: Clarify committed replay and shared evidence target forms
acceptance: New operations revalidate the current target revisions and required confirmation. An already committed semantic retry recovers only its permitted receipt through the existing scoped replay rules. Both human and AI requests can select an identified workspace object or explicitly clear selection, and omission of the target is rejected.

plan.outcome: A caller can recover a lost committed response after its revisions advance and can select or explicitly clear any supported evidence target under its current grant.
hypotheses: The 1.1 target union already supports workspace objects and null. The established replay authorization applies before evaluating new-work revision and confirmation preconditions.

risks.failure: A retry is rejected just because the original commit advanced a revision, or it discloses the earlier result after access was revoked.
One caller rejects a workspace object or accepts an omitted target as an explicit clear.

plan.rollback: Retain the accepted 1.1 schema, receipts and examples. Fix only the normative cross-references and examples if an implementation precondition conflicts.

non_goals: Implement durable operations, generalize grants, or publish a release. Runtime transaction ordering is an M2-001 acceptance case.

preserve: The 1.1 target union, scoped idempotency key and current disclosure rules.
change: Describe committed-retry ordering, all shared target families and explicit clearing consistently.
evolution.data_plan: No stored data or wire format changes.
evolution.cleanup: Remove ambiguous new-work wording from the receipt recovery and object-selection paths.

tasks.title: Verify replay admission and completion against their separate deadlines
acceptance: The ordinary chart renders both known candle updates through an admitted real worker stream when a valid history preparation pushes total elapsed time beyond the former five-second browser expectation.

Bounded checks separately identify admission and terminal failures. A successful run still requires the correct intermediate and final candle paints, frozen row, exact frames, and one admitted subscription. Unexpected failed requests cannot count as a successful replay.

Real retries and epoch-gap reads in the quality journey observe a separate preparation boundary. A prior gap still clears on retry, and failed or gapped streams cannot satisfy a completed-replay assertion.

plan.outcome: Diagnose the actual failing Ubuntu assertion, then verify the complete real replay under bounded preparation latency while keeping application timeouts and frame checks effective.
hypotheses: The browser waited five seconds for preparation and an entire subscription together. Each operation has its own application deadline and a slow valid preparation can exhaust the single assertion.

risks.failure: A hung operation or unexpected failed subscription becomes indistinguishable from legitimate admission delay.
A completed message hides a missed intermediate render or a mutation to frozen history.

plan.rollback: Retain the failed Ubuntu log and screenshot from run 44504564860. If a stage exceeds its actual application deadline, use the phase evidence to repair that specific path.

non_goals: Product retry policy, source data, credentials and Windows desktop acceptance.

preserve: Observed worker frames, visual values, cancellation and frozen historical rows.
change: Diagnose preparation, stream entry and completion at their actual boundaries.
evolution.data_plan: Only synthetic test traffic and existing diagnostic evidence are used.
evolution.cleanup: Keep one streamed acceptance path and the existing worker deadlines. Retain reproducible evidence of delayed preparation.

tasks.title: Verify offline chart restoration across catalog, history and paint
acceptance: An unconfigured start makes no market request. Explicit sample selection and restoration read the real catalog and requested synthetic history in order. The restored view identifies the selected source, instrument, timeframe and frozen data.

A delayed but valid catalog and history restore the chosen layout, forty bars and original last close without starting another subscription. An unsuccessful operation or missing render fails its own bounded check.

plan.outcome: Verify the visible chart after an explicit sample is reopened, including a cold catalog and history load.
hypotheses: Windows completed the replay and later captured the restored chart. The reload assertion started its five-second render budget before the two serial reads had completed.

risks.failure: A missing, failed or unrelated operation satisfies the restoration check.
The restored chart shows the replay projection, loses the explicit source or automatically replays.

plan.rollback: Keep the original Windows run and the controlled local failure. Compare the operation and render evidence before changing application policy.

non_goals: Changes to the chart renderer, market data, application resource limits or release status.

preserve: User-selected sample restoration, frozen data, chart rendering and subscription lifecycle.
change: Start the render assertion after the independent catalog and history reads.
evolution.data_plan: The regression uses synthetic fixtures on loopback.
evolution.cleanup: Keep a single live path for restoration and use ordinary UI assertions after its bounded reads.

tasks.title: Verify recovery boundaries and owned worker interruption on Windows
acceptance: A cold native Windows runner can verify recovery, preserve a visible gap on mismatched replacement and exhaust the bounded retry sequence while preserving the expected terminal cause. Independent request, cleanup and cancellation limits remain enforced.

The real chart interruption reaches only the admitted worker under the test-owned preview. The test observes its confirmed progress, one final projection and unchanged frozen data. Closed-bar browser checks observe preparation and stream progress separately and still reject every altered or incomplete frame.
The hosted change verification leaves enough bounded time for the full Windows check sequence and retained evidence, including failures. Linux and native Windows outcomes are observed separately.
A provisioned Linux runner launches the pinned Chromium before the chart suites. When required system libraries are absent, install them and verify the same browser starts before continuing.

Default sample startup verifies the completed catalog and its subsequent history before asserting the chart. The real interrupted worker resumes inside the original product budget, and the minimal locked dependency environment enforces every format declared by the protocol and project schemas.

plan.outcome: One credible cross-platform verification of owned replay interruption and closed-bar repair, with diagnostics retained after failed checks.
hypotheses: The Windows redirector adds a process between the helper and its owning Node test. Cold worker startup, retries and browser preparation can individually succeed while a check waiting across them expires.

Runs 44520641312 and 44521481949 stopped fetching Ubuntu font packages before executing any project check. Starting the pinned browser verifies the existing host runtime and reserves package installation for missing dependencies.

The native Windows runner observed reconnecting and resumed before the real stream timed out. The optional schema extra compiles an unused grammar on every worker start. Compare fresh locked environments with the same owned bridge, fixture and monotonic deadlines.

risks.failure: An unrelated process is interrupted or a late/absent result is reported as acceptable.
A blanket delay masks a stalled worker, invalid replacement or unbounded recovery.
Removing an optional grammar silently disables a format the wire protocol or project evidence uses, or a chart startup assertion waits across multiple cold operations.

plan.rollback: Retain the cancelled hosted run and its surviving check tails. Exercise controlled missing, delayed or incorrect results before accepting replacement evidence.

non_goals: New market sources, chart features or release qualification.

preserve: Retry limits, confirmed stream position, frozen source data, private process ownership and an observable terminal error.
change: Bind test observation to actual admitted work and keep the hosted Windows report recoverable under cold builds.
evolution.data_plan: Private CI diagnostics and temporary synthetic fixtures cover the regression.
evolution.cleanup: Keep one restart sequence and one test-owned process tree. Leave unverified hosted results visible.

tasks.title: Verify the persisted timeframe and eligible undo across local workspace sessions
acceptance: A fresh browser and restarted Rust writer restore the committed timeframe, discover the eligible local undo, and restore the original timeframe exactly once. Independent profiles and rejected callers cannot read or mutate another workspace.

An ordinary unconfigured launch stays inert. The opted-in local host binds the trusted profile, actor, workspace and database. Actual Rust process and desktop bridge tests cover durable effects. Built UI tests verify native IPC arguments and error handling using a substituted transport.
The harness exercises the two named checks, records their distinct evidence, validates dependency inventory and retains synthetic verification artifacts.

plan.outcome: A repeatable, bounded acceptance of the first local workspace write and undo across process and browser restarts.
hypotheses: A new browser can use the core operation log to discover an eligible undo after a writer restart. The scoped result is independent of browser storage and the synthetic market source.

risks.failure: A restarted client repeats a write, trusts another profile, loses the undo or receives permission from an earlier invocation.
A native transport substitute accidentally counts as an actual native runtime or an unconfigured host gains a new grant.
Only one host can execute the regression or its artifacts include the working data directory.
A local caller receives another launcher grant, profile storage is created under shared filesystem permissions, or a live writer returns a stale cached snapshot after a concurrent commit.

plan.rollback: Keep each fixture in an isolated temporary local profile. Preserve failed run evidence and correct the failing boundary before recording completion.

non_goals: Decision-note retention, backup restoration, full production profile selection and packaged Windows experience remain assigned to their owning tasks.

preserve: One Rust authorization path, local data ownership and synthetic source opt-in.
change: Verify the eligible undo from fresh local sessions and independently exercise both application transports.
evolution.data_plan: Only temporary synthetic profiles are used for the browser checks. They are removed after their owned processes exit.
evolution.cleanup: Keep the process probe test-only. Stage named browser results and retain private working databases locally.

tasks.title: Verify serial catalog and history startup in chart previews
acceptance: Default sample startup verifies the exact real catalog and history requests and their separate successful replies before checking chart readiness in both browser suites.
Holding each real reply independently reproduces a startup beyond the old five-second aggregate wait. Exact chart, replay, offline retry, and typed worker-error assertions still apply.

plan.outcome: Separate catalog and history verification from chart paint in the inherited M1-001 browser paths.
hypotheses: The two serial worker reads can legitimately outlast the former five-second render wait, including after Retry demo.

risks.failure: An unsuccessful worker reply, incorrect series, or missing chart passes as slow startup.

plan.rollback: Retain hosted run 44531620190 and the held-response regression before reopening any failing phase.

non_goals: Worker deadlines, application retry rules, fixtures, and packaged Windows acceptance.

preserve: Explicit synthetic opt-in, replay and chart values, and offline recovery behavior.
change: Use the shared default startup verifier and cover two independently held real replies and a typed worker failure.
evolution.data_plan: Use only committed synthetic fixtures through the local bridge.
evolution.cleanup: Keep timeout allowances in browser verification and leave product deadlines intact.

tasks.title: Isolate the live publisher advisory request in GitHub verification
acceptance: Hosted verification uses the existing job read token only for the exact approved public publisher advisory GET. No redirect or other dependency client receives it.

The live published advisory is bound to the current job attempt and checkout. Missing, unavailable, stale, malformed, or changed metadata fails review. Inventory, notices, immutable Actions, OSV, npm, and target-scope requirements still apply.

plan.outcome: Recheck the public publisher advisory under the existing CI identity without transmitting it elsewhere.
hypotheses: The Linux runner exhausted its anonymous GitHub REST request quota. A job-scoped authenticated read can avoid that quota when the publisher endpoint accepts the identity.

risks.failure: A redirect, later check, subprocess, or diagnostic receives the token.
An unavailable, stale, or changed publisher reply authorizes a disposition.

plan.rollback: Retain the run 44536924867 failure. If the approved live endpoint remains unavailable, keep the gate failed and retain its bounded diagnostics.

non_goals: Permission expansion, user credentials, product changes, and static advisory waivers.

preserve: Existing online advisory, target coverage, license, and notice acceptance.
change: Isolate an exact-origin publisher fetch and bind its public result to the current CI invocation.
evolution.data_plan: Store only reviewed public advisory fields in the runner temporary directory.
evolution.cleanup: The fetch has no child checks. The runner owns temporary public evidence and the built-in job credential lifetime.

tasks.title: Own browser response waits in the workspace preview harness
acceptance: A controlled initial document failure in real Chromium reports its navigation error and releases the pending workspace snapshot observation before context teardown.

Response and download observations in the workspace suite are scoped to the browser action. Test-only HTTP probes consume or cancel the bodies they own. Existing success and rejection assertions continue to pass without retries or extended timeouts.
Retain the original hosted Windows error and report the harness finding separately from the unresolved origin of that Chromium navigation error.

plan.outcome: A real navigation error remains the primary assertion failure and leaves no workspace snapshot observer behind.
hypotheses: The response promise created before navigation was observed only after successful navigation and UI assertions. Closing the context on failure rejects that abandoned promise.

risks.failure: A snapshot listener survives a rejected action or captures the wrong response.
A test helper masks the original document error or changes a notes authorization assertion.

plan.rollback: Keep the original hosted failure and the controlled red result. Scope any repair to the workspace harness and compare the original operation assertions.

non_goals: Changes to product operations, grants, SQLite, public registries, timeouts or runner settings.
open_questions: The origin of the isolated hosted Chromium document error remains unverified.

preserve: Real Chromium, Vite, Rust persistence, the existing test deadlines, and independent synthetic profiles.
change: Tie the lifetimes of test observations and response bodies to the operations that own them.
evolution.data_plan: Use a unique local port and a controlled browser route or temporary synthetic profile.
evolution.cleanup: Detach pending listeners when an action fails. Consume or cancel owned HTTP response bodies and close the owned browser contexts.

tasks.title: Isolate the offline sample timeframe from the durable workspace
acceptance: Through the real preview and Rust writer, an explicitly opened and labeled simulated sample can save 5m and restore it on refresh while the bound workspace retains its independent 1m revision and existing undo receipt.

Leaving the sample in the launched page restores the durable controls and permits the original undo through the fragment-scrubbed in-memory grant. Refreshing the scrubbed shell requires a new handoff to use durable controls.

The built desktop UI with opted-in substituted Tauri IPC routes sample controls to the sample preference and retains the private timeframe and undo on return. Unconfigured startup remains inert and keeps explicit sample opt-in.

plan.outcome: The active synthetic chart and private workspace have independent timeframe ownership across entry, leave and browser reload.
hypotheses: The composed chart binds the local workspace controls while the sample is active. Giving the active source ownership of the controls keeps both stored states independent.

risks.failure: Opening the sample changes a durable revision or replaces the existing private undo.
Leaving or refreshing the sample loses the expected timeframe, activates a private grant in a new browser document, or loses the grant in the original launched document.

plan.rollback: Retain red and green runs using isolated synthetic profiles. Revert the UI routing change on the task branch if the ordinary durable path or synthetic startup regresses.

non_goals: Private decision notes, evidence selection, general operation replay, profile backup and migration recovery continue under their own development scope.
Keep the existing SQLite schema and local authorization contract. Native IPC substitution and portable Rust bridge tests leave installed Windows WebView acceptance to its own gate.

preserve: Explicit sample opt-in, existing sample preference format and leave behavior.
Private snapshot, durable write and undo through the same Rust registry and profile store.
Page-local preview grants and unconfigured startup without a private write path.
change: Bind chart controls and sample reads to the selected source while retaining the existing local workspace session in the parent UI.
evolution.data_plan: Reuse the public sample preference. Use temporary synthetic SQLite profiles for verification.
evolution.cleanup: Remove generated synthetic profiles after their writers exit. Retain red and green reports with synthetic observations and keep launch grants out of artifacts.

tasks.title: Route delegated Herdr work through bounded approval policies
acceptance: The normal Herdr launcher sends implementation and coordination tasks to the automatic approval reviewer with the workspace-write sandbox. Review tasks use the read-only sandbox and return a denial directly. Both paths preserve the assigned checkout, model, reasoning effort and literal task.

Exercise the installed CLI through a real local Herdr session in a synthetic or task worktree. Retain the effective arguments and an independently checked outcome. Keep approval refusals visible to the coordinator.

plan.outcome: A bounded development assignment can finish routine work without a developer at each child terminal.
hypotheses: The launcher inherited interactive approvals for implementation and coordination. The installed CLI supports automatic review in its normal workspace sandbox.

risks.failure: A writer silently gains unrestricted access or a reviewer becomes writable.
A real policy refusal is hidden, or quoting the assignment changes its meaning.

plan.rollback: Preserve the previous launcher commit and incomplete assignments in their existing worktrees. If the chosen CLI mode is unavailable, report the terminal failure and retain the task.

non_goals: Changing global Codex settings, extending product-user permissions, or publishing a release.

preserve: Role-specific models, read-only review, current worktree selection, verbatim assignments, and the explicit local Herdr space.
change: Route elevated development requests to the built-in automatic reviewer. Surface denials and missing inputs directly.
evolution.data_plan: Use repository code and synthetic local probes. The launcher does not persist credentials or user content.
evolution.cleanup: Only newly started sessions receive new launch arguments. Preserve pending work and retire coordinator-owned test sessions after verification.

tasks.title: Verify first native sample startup and its isolation from a private workspace
acceptance: An ordinary Windows development WebView opens the explicitly selected offline sample, displays the correct futures bars at 1m and 5m, and restores the 5m simulated chart in a new process. The same account retains the prior private workspace and can undo the original private change.

Retain the first native failure. Record the real executable, worker environment, observations and any unconfirmed cause. Compare relevant runtime changes in the same standard-user guest using the real default catalog and history requests.
Verify the shipped combination of source and pinned runtime through the normal entry, preserve schema format checks, worker cleanup, and existing production deadlines.

plan.outcome: The normal private desktop can enter, persist and exit an explicit local sample without losing its original private undo.
hypotheses: The old worker environment imports a format grammar that lengthens startup. The first GUI failure reported a timeout before the catalog appeared. Its underlying mechanism has not yet been isolated.

risks.failure: A faster partial run masks loss of the sample preference, the private undo, or a terminal worker error.
Changing the validator dependencies drops an actively used wire format or leaves inconsistent locks.

plan.rollback: Keep the original executable, dependency lock, local guest artifacts and synthetic profiles. Restore the previous runtime after each diagnostic comparison.

non_goals: Packaged distribution, physical-device experience and connected model sessions have separate gates.
open_questions: Which native stage exceeded its budget during the original first launch?

preserve: Offline sample opt-in, its simulated badge and independent saved preferences.
Private workspace revisions, original undo receipts, configured format checks and bounded worker operations.
change: Qualify the normal native sample startup on the integrated runtime and remove measured avoidable cold work.
evolution.data_plan: Use only synthetic market data and an isolated development profile in a disposable Windows clone.
evolution.cleanup: Close owned processes and retain the original source, runtime and diagnostic results separately.

tasks.title: Observe cold preview module startup and report terminal failures
acceptance: Verify that an ordinary loopback navigation mounts the unconfigured chart before the quality test opens its controls and sends zero market operations before opt-in.
A deliberately failed or unavailable first application module must fail startup within its own bounded stage, with the observed terminal reason and without navigation retries.
Retain the hosted failure and distinguish a locally reproduced readiness defect from any unresolved Windows-specific cause.
tasks.closure_reason: The bounded readiness and terminal diagnostics passed the local harness. The hosted Windows startup incident remains open until a later instrumented run exposes its terminal reason.

plan.outcome: A market quality check verifies a rendered chart before interacting with Data sources and reports the first observable startup failure instead of waiting for an absent control.
hypotheses: The artifact shows an unmounted chart before any market selection. HTML navigation alone cannot establish whether the application module loaded and React rendered.
The artifact does not identify a failed module, JavaScript exception, or browser/host fault. A controlled module fault can verify the harness separately from the unresolved Windows cause.

risks.failure: A failed or hung app mount is treated as a pass, retried invisibly, or lost in a whole-test locator timeout.
A startup diagnostic exposes uncontrolled URLs or replaces the real market checks.

plan.rollback: Retain run 44546526143 and the controlled failures. Revert any unverified runtime change and keep the Windows observation open.

non_goals: Production retries or timeout changes, chart behavior changes, packaged Windows acceptance, and assuming a root cause from a screenshot.
open_questions: Which first-page event caused the unmounted chart on the hosted Windows runner?

preserve: Real loopback chart boot and worker operations, default no-market-call checks, and all quality assertions.
change: Separate page navigation from observable application readiness and preserve bounded diagnostics on a terminal startup failure.
evolution.data_plan: Use only synthetic test content and same-origin resource classifications.
evolution.cleanup: Detach startup observers after the readiness outcome and leave the test browser to its existing teardown.

tasks.title: Report sample startup transport terminals and isolate injected recovery controls
acceptance: The shared startup check reports an observed navigation failure, catalog or history transport failure, or rejected operation during that stage, without automatic retries or changes to market UI failure behavior.

Verify one unmodified loopback baseline through the ordinary catalog, history, preparation and replay. Reuse same-run synthetic responses for exact matching futures requests in injected protocol controls, preserving every protocol assertion and the real stock replacement.
Run real closed-bar repair and worker interruption checks. Retain the hosted incident and state which underlying connection cause and Windows verification remain unresolved.
tasks.closure_reason: The Linux task harness verified the diagnostic regression, shared synthetic baseline and both real recovery gates. The original hosted connection cause remains unconfirmed, and this revision has not run on Windows.

plan.outcome: Expose the actual startup terminal and make injected recovery coverage independent of repeated worker startups.
hypotheses: The hosted workspace mounted and then lost catalog startup. Response-only polling hides a Playwright requestfailed terminal.
The injected protocol controls can share an exact same-run synthetic baseline while real loopback and recovery coverage remain independent.

risks.failure: Navigation, a transport failure, or a non-BUSY rejection is reported as a generic stage deadline.
A fixture masks request drift or replaces real recovery or interruption evidence.

plan.rollback: Retain the original hosted failure and staged negative evidence. Keep real gates unchanged if fixture isolation cannot preserve their coverage.

non_goals: Production connection policies, retries, market data changes and packaged Windows acceptance.
open_questions: The published Windows artifacts do not establish which connection error occurred.

preserve: Financial assertions, request sequencing, exact BUSY admission, frozen provenance and both real recovery gates.
change: Observe early terminal outcomes during startup and capture one verified loopback baseline for the injected futures cases.
evolution.data_plan: Keep only same-run synthetic responses in test worker memory and use ordinary sanitized reports.
evolution.cleanup: Close the baseline page and its context after capture. Let Playwright dispose of each case's routes and fixture context.

tasks.title: Show workspace startup and offer manual recovery before the application mounts
acceptance: An already delivered desktop or preview document shows an accessible startup state when its application entry fails or remains pending. The user can explicitly reload the same location and reach the ordinary workspace once the entry is available.

A healthy mount replaces the startup state. Failed and pending entries issue zero market operations and perform no automatic navigation. Startup verification still requires a real chart workspace and reports its original terminal failure.
Retain the original hosted screenshot and distinguish the historical trigger from the verified rendered-document behavior.
tasks.closure_reason: The delivered startup panel, manual reload, module failure and ordinary chart journey passed on hosted Ubuntu and Windows in run 44573777675. The mechanism behind the earlier blank Windows screenshot remains undetermined.

plan.outcome: A person can see and recover from an unmounted workspace even while its main JavaScript module is unavailable.
hypotheses: The HTML document currently supplies an empty root. A controlled failure of the first application module leaves no visible workspace or recovery action. The old hosted screenshot alone cannot identify a particular failed request.

risks.failure: The startup notice is mistaken for a mounted chart or causes background navigation, market traffic or an opaque error.
Reload loses the current location or the fallback remains in the loaded application.

plan.rollback: Keep the bounded diagnostic tests and earlier failure reports. Revert the startup markup and helper together if ordinary mounting regresses.

non_goals: Replacing the desktop host, increasing worker timeouts or diagnosing the historical Windows incident from a screenshot.

preserve: The active URL, explicit sample opt-in, default idle workspace, existing Content Security Policy and independent market worker deadlines.

tasks.title: Diagnose the Windows timeout test log sharing failure
acceptance: Retain the failed main Windows diagnostic and distinguish a verification-process handle leak from delayed or external file release.
Verify bounded process cleanup and intact partial diagnostics on Windows. Resolve the observed sharing failure without suppressing errors.

plan.outcome: A native Windows timeout leaves readable partial output, stops owned writers within the cleanup bound and allows the fixture to be removed. Retained evidence records what the original failure and the focused experiment each establish.
hypotheses: A Windows virtual environment redirector may start the real launcher before the redirector is assigned to the job, leaving that launcher outside the job.
Job accounting may reach zero before a descendant's process object signals and its inherited output handle closes.
A separate file opener could allow the successful report reads while preventing deletion. The original traceback does not identify the holder.

risks.failure: A cleanup change hides persistent file contention or returns while a descendant can still write after the report digest is recorded.
The repair replaces the separate contract branch's product focus or loses the failing diagnostic.

non_goals: Product behavior, provider calls, private records, release and changes to the contract pull request.

evolution.data_plan: Use synthetic files and retain the original authenticated failure report and logs by digest. No application storage changes.
evolution.cleanup: Join any test-owned processes and close observation handles. Keep final deletion strict and retain failed observations before switching approaches.

tasks.closure_reason: Ubuntu and native Windows passed the selected checks in run 44996898959. The venv redirector control placed the actual gate outside the verification job. The direct interpreter gate entered that job. Although the writer handle was still unsignaled when job accounting reached zero, it was signaled on return from the full timeout cleanup, 0.266 seconds from the timed wait. The delete-access probe, partial output and digest, and strict deletion passed. The independent reader control reproduced WinError 32 until release. The historical file holder remains unknown.

tasks.title: Join observed Windows verification Job members before returning
acceptance: Retain the exact PR failure where the live writer's process handle was unsignaled at timeout return while DELETE access already succeeded.

hypotheses: Waiting for the gate and zero active Job members can finish before a separately observed writer signals. Native run 44997698442 observed this at the public timeout return, with DELETE access already available.

risks.failure: A process ID that exited before inspection could be reused, or cleanup could extend a separate deadline per member.

plan.rollback: Retain both original failed diagnostics. Revert the additional cleanup change on this repair branch or through a reviewed correction, preserving the independently verified gate assignment fix.

non_goals: Product changes, provider calls, private input, release and historical file-holder attribution.
open_questions: Which return boundaries now see the same writer signal on the hosted native runner?

tasks.closure_reason: Ubuntu and Windows passed the selected checks in run 45000485659. Windows confirmed that the live writer was in the verification Job and that its retained handle signaled before WindowsJob.stop and run_logged returned. The timeout returned 0.266 seconds from the start of the timed wait. DELETE access, partial output, digest and strict deletion all passed. The exit barrier covers verified snapshot members.
