tasks.title: Reap browser verification servers when their check ends
acceptance: Exercise the ordinary check execution entry with a detached listener and a distinct unowned listener. After normal exit, failure, cancellation and timeout, the owned listener can be rebound, the unrelated listener still replies and the original outcome is retained.
Run the ordinary desktop localization check with the repository deadlines and a fresh port. Retain the original failed Linux report and the ownership and port observations.
Verify the task checks and preserve the existing Linux market supervisor and Windows job behavior through the same public execution entry.
Require explicit supervisor confirmation of finished cleanup across parent SIGCHLD dispositions, and record a late interruption after bounded cleanup.
Publish a bounded stable snapshot before digesting the ordinary log when Linux cleanup is unconfirmed. Keep the failed diagnosis and a verified retry independently resolvable.
Record an interrupt arriving during serial log finalization and preserve any existing cleanup failure. Retain the terminal row, durable run report and ordinary stop behavior.
A real SIGINT at a blocked console result write promptly stops output without losing its terminal row, log digest, original and latest reports or independent retry.

On the actual parallel entry, one SIGINT releases a full shared Linux pipe whether a second writer fills it before or after readiness. Preserve caller descriptor flags, terminal outcomes, original and latest reports, and a separate retry.
Reach the real Windows gate identity and Job Object membership assertions with a fixture that preserves the runtime platform and both interpreter choices.

plan.outcome: An ordinary Linux browser check releases every process in its own server tree and its port when verification finishes, including when the check times out.
hypotheses: Only the market recovery check requests the Linux subreaper. The ordinary localization launcher starts descendants in separate sessions, which survive process-group cleanup.
The early command result currently substitutes for cleanup evidence when the parent automatically reaps the supervisor. A late SIGINT can escape the final wait.
A residual inherited writer can still mutate the original log inode after unconfirmed cleanup.
The serial digest and terminal result phase currently has no interrupt handling after the check runner returns.
Console emission currently precedes admission of terminal rows and is not part of durable report publication.
Pipe readiness does not reserve capacity for a later write. A cooperative flag cannot interrupt an already blocking write.
The Windows gate fixture dropped the runtime platform when substituting the interpreter paths. The runner branches on platform before it invokes either gate.

risks.failure: A browser command or indirect browser launcher can again outlive its check or occupy a later check port.
A cleanup operation reaches an unrelated process or masks a real timeout, command failure or cleanup failure.
The parent accepts an early, missing or incomplete cleanup result as a pass after supervisor failure.
A first interruption during teardown drops the check row or leaves owned descendants without confirming cleanup.
A live writer mutates published evidence, or continuous output, partial reads or interruption make the snapshot unbounded or misleading.
An interrupt during log finalization loses the terminal result, overwrites a cleanup failure, or allows a later selected check to start.
A blocked console write drops a finished row, continues to later checks, or blocks again during tail, report summary or recovery output.
A competing writer invalidates readiness, nonblocking flags leak to the caller, or partial output loses or duplicates bytes.
A stale Windows fixture prevents the redirector and normal gate controls from exercising process identity or containment.

plan.rollback: Keep the failed original and port observation. If the shared supervisor changes existing exit semantics, restore the previous path and retain the active finding until a bounded repair passes.

non_goals: Product data and market worker behavior, individual test deadlines, user-managed servers and release qualification.
open_questions: Which registered check commands own detachable process trees, and can one shared execution rule cover future additions?

preserve: Original per-check output, exit codes, genuine timeouts, independent verification processes and Windows job ownership.
change: Apply process-tree lifetime ownership at the Linux verification boundary that runs the affected commands.
Separate command readiness from final cleanup confirmation, and complete bounded teardown after a late interruption.
Detach the published diagnostic inode from unconfirmed Linux output writers while retaining the existing archive bindings.
Carry a serial finalization interrupt into the ordinary check result and run report.
Handle blocked console interruption independently of row admission and persist the original and latest reports without relying on stdout.
Use owned nonblocking pipe output for the Linux cooperative console and retry only unwritten bytes.
Preserve the native runtime attributes when overriding only the test gate interpreter paths.
evolution.data_plan: No persisted product data changes. Exercise synthetic local listeners and retain the original check diagnostics.
evolution.cleanup: Release test-owned processes and compare port ownership against an independent live listener. Retain raw diagnostic and regression logs.

tasks.closure_reason: Linux and Windows passed the four scoped checks and their ordinary PR jobs. Independent review exercised the process identity contrast and the blocked-pipe interruption controls. Windows ran the assigned-process, timeout and external-reader tests. Linux ran the descendant cleanup and competing-writer checks and retained terminal results and their original logs. The earlier failed Windows runs and prior receipts remain available.

tasks.title: Verify peer lock ownership across a slow interrupted console check
acceptance: Retain the protected failure and identical-tree passing control. Establish whether the peer exited independently before the last running-stage assertion by observing its lifetime and lock.

Exercise one SIGINT during blocked console output with a live, unrelated owner and a deliberately released lock as a rejected control. Verify reports, original bytes, retry and cleanup across all seven existing scenarios, including an interaction outlasting the previous helper window.

If the controller exits early, its owned fixture exits and releases its lock. Preserve the existing check deadlines, reject a lost witness and retain a successful ordinary Linux run of the corrected source.
tasks.closure_reason: The corrected Linux test passed all seven SIGINT stages in the ordinary PR and exact-source task workflows. A slow control retained the unrelated lock beyond the old deadline and an early-release control failed the expected assertion. Both original native failures remain archived. Their peer exit reasons were not recorded.

plan.outcome: A slow interrupted check verifies a live independent lock holder for the entire interaction and releases its owned fixture on every exit.
hypotheses: The protected log identifies only the failed acquisition assertion. On the exact original fixture, holding the final blocked console past 30 seconds reproduced the peer exiting normally and exposing the lock before SIGINT. The same protected sequence can therefore fail even when the check leaves unrelated processes alone.

risks.failure: The assertion passes without a live independent owner or rejects a healthy slow check.
A helper inherits a lifetime handle or remains alive after a failing parent, leaving a lock or process behind.

plan.rollback: Retain the native failure and restore the previous witness if lock isolation, cancellation outcomes or fixture cleanup regress.

non_goals: Changes to product records, the production timeout policy or the Windows verification schedule.
open_questions: Can the corrected peer survive a console interaction past the old fallback and release immediately when its owning controller closes the pipe or dies, including when other children remain alive?

preserve: Single-SIGINT report publication, owned-child cleanup, lock isolation, healthy retries and the existing process bounds.
change: Give only the test controller the peer stdin writer. Verify clean exit and lock release on EOF while keeping the seven public stages, their SIGINT bound and their report assertions.
evolution.data_plan: Use temporary locks, pipes and synthetic verification files. Retain both original CI reports.
evolution.cleanup: Reap the test-owned peer on normal and early exits. Verify that other processes and original reports survive the interrupted check.

tasks.title: Distinguish refused indicator status reads during delivery recovery
acceptance: The full, cropped and lost-delivery indicator journeys exercise the actual workspace. When a status read is explicitly refused before admission, the observable result, original admitted task, bounded delivery recovery and user-visible exhaustion remain correct.

The verification records every raw draft, preview, status and cancellation. An extra admitted status recovery, a new or repeated preview submission, a wrong-task read and an ambiguous refusal cannot satisfy the same-task recovery assertion.
Retain the original Windows admission sequence, the focused positive and rejected controls, and a passing ordinary Windows exercise of the corrected candidate.

Native preview status retries only an explicitly refused writer admission. An admitted registry or storage BUSY, an older unclassified reply and an unrelated native error stop and cancel the original task.
The first-window journal rejects a raw cancellation with no task ID. A valid previous-task cancellation and the cancellation on exhaustion remain accounted for.
tasks.closure_reason: On the ordinary PR and scoped workflows, Linux and Windows each delivered nine browser journals from seven frozen-preview scenarios and four native transport controls. After losing a ready reply, the bounded held route observed two explicit refusals, the unforwarded request reaching its original browser deadline, and one cancellation of the same task. Full and cropped windows returned zero volatility. The earlier protected run retained two request identities without their HTTP outcomes.

plan.outcome: Preserve bounded same-task recovery and make the native zero-volatility observation distinguish a definite pre-admission refusal from a second accepted status recovery.
hypotheses: The Windows two-loss trial received one explicit HTTP 429 BUSY and one lost HTTP 200 ready response after the original ready delivery reset. The existing raw length assertion counted both as recovery attempts.

Real Windows and Linux controls separate the original ready delivery reset, an authenticated HTTP 429 before writer admission and the next admitted read. Each status attempt owns a distinct wire ID for the same task.

The old polling loop retried any BUSY, including HTTP 200 after admission. Use the existing transport admission signal and preserve both the total polling deadline and the single allowed frozen status delivery recovery.
The native writer lock can be acquired before an application or SQLite BUSY is returned. Only the pre-lock failure can attest to refusal.
With no previous task, equality against an undefined task ID can hide an invalid raw cancellation.
The browser can abandon a last intercepted synthetic request at the polling deadline before a refusal becomes observable. The original transport failure alone cannot establish delivery or admission.

risks.failure: A count based only on admitted or unique task IDs hides duplicate status, draft or preview operations, or permits requests for another task.
Changing the evidence predicate admits a malformed or ambiguous refusal, misses a duplicate cancellation or alters the full and cropped results.

Treating an admitted native storage error or an older unclassified reply as pre-admission reissues a status read. Moving the signal outside the writer lock boundary also risks changing other workspace and protocol replies.
An unscoped cancellation is treated as past-task cleanup, or rejecting it disrupts real previous-task or exhaustion cleanup.
A terminal request with ambiguous transport, wrong task, earlier position or possible upstream admission is hidden as a refusal or accepted recovery; an assertion drops the complete bounded journal.

plan.rollback: Retain both native reports, their raw request journals and the historical strict replay controls. Restore the prior assertion if the admission boundary cannot be identified.

non_goals: Expanding operation authority, changing the preview result or increasing the recovery allowance or deadline.
open_questions: Which reliable response fields prove rejection before the same-task status operation is admitted, and how is its request identity related to subsequent polling?

preserve: Exact admitted task and artifact, finite delivery recovery, all raw outbound operations, cancellation and honest visible failure.
change: Qualify the first demonstrated mismatch between a definite refusal and the recovery assertion at its owning entry.
Separate a terminal browser deadline on a never-forwarded test route from observed HTTP refusal, admitted status and ambiguous transport outcomes.
evolution.data_plan: Use the accepted synthetic frozen chart and isolated workspace. Retain response status, operation identity and synthetic results.
evolution.cleanup: Release response controls, close owned windows and reap the portable writer on every path.

A fresh independent AI with the normal entry receives no expected answers. Retain its own response, the exact source and contrasting controls, along with required task checks.

Ordinary overview and handoff end the engagement only after each workstream has an explicit accepted observation for its owner-defined criteria. A single acceptance leaves the other action open. Negative or missing observations cannot validate a declared closure.
A new coordinator can execute the source commands emitted through the read-only overview and handoff under an unwritable package cache and read the owner terms and any accepted closure.

Corrections on da5fd0a6 passed the task harness and independent review. The cold original is retained at archives/observations/repo-hygiene-20261125/m0-158-fresh-handoff-683c949a/original-response.jsonl. Both owner workstreams remain open.

hypotheses: The prior handoff preserved assignment identities but did not put the owner-defined end conditions on the restore path. Replaying operational tasks and reading the ordinary protected focus alone allowed an intermediate result to be reported as completion. Confirm the exact failure boundary in an unprompted fresh session.

The dated owner record is reachable through the narrow repair while that task is focused. Closing the repair removes that route. Compare an explicit successor pointer with project-level engagement state by switching to a genuine audit successor and then ending the engagement.

The common engagement loader verifies identity and observation text but infers acceptance from their presence. The earlier positive fixtures omitted a disposition. Correctly digested rejected, incomplete and accepted observations distinguish evidence identity from acceptance at the public views.

The overview selects pinned Python, but the handoff invocation loses the read-only mode. Earlier controls extracted arguments or translated the launcher. Execute the exact emitted handoff and source commands with an unwritable uv cache and compare the returned records.

A repair overloads routine context, assumes private transcripts exist on every host or silently changes unrelated product scope.
Closing the repair or changing focus hides either open commitment, or a partial or unproven closure permits premature stop while later product work inherits maintenance scope.
A digest-valid rejected or incomplete closure can end the engagement before the workstream meets the owner terms.
A pinned read-only handoff can return an owner or closure source command whose package launcher requires a writable cache.

plan.rollback: Keep the authenticated original pause and owner records, restore the prior navigation and use the explicit authoritative workstream reference while verifying the repair.

non_goals: Product runtime operations, public publication of private transcripts, or a requirement to retain every development conversation.

preserve: Existing status, focused context, protected checks, task scope and evidence identities.
change: Make the two ongoing commitments reconstructible on the normal coordinator route with separate observed state and closure.
Keep the engagement discoverable beyond the focus repair. Derive its stop state from independently recorded acceptance for each workstream.

Retain the focus-independent loader and shared command formatter. The independent successor control supports the engagement boundary. Validate the observation's explicit acceptance in that loader and carry the read-only mode from overview to handoff and its source commands. The two failures involve those existing boundaries and require no separate registry, source or migration.
